stem:
Tanya has two sticks of lengths $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $11\,\mathrm{cm}$. She wants a third stick of length $x\,\mathrm{cm}$ so the three lengths can form a triangle.

Which two claims correctly describe the allowed values of $x$?

options.text: The answer is the phrase fixed side lengths, naming that phrase instead of giving a range for $x$.
$x$ must satisfy $5 < x < 17$, because $|11-6| < x < 11+6$ with the endpoints excluded.
Any length strictly between the difference and the sum of $6$ and $11$ can be the third side.
She must first construct the triangle with compass arcs, and only then decide which $x$ values are allowed.

teacher.key_rationale: Triangle inequality needs |11-6|<x<11+6, so 5<x<17. Naming fixed sides alone, or requiring a compass construction before the range, leave the inequality hinge.
